To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic exposure thickened the adsorbed water layer on mica surface in aqueous solution of structure-disordering ions, such as K+, Rb+, Cs+, and NH4+.
the thickness of adsorbed layer can be directly measured using AFM and that the magnetic exposure increases the adsorbed thickness of the layer in aqueous electrolyte solutions.

the thickness of the electrical double layer on a mica surface in aqueous electrolyte solutions is thickened by the magnetic exposure, and that the magnetic effects are observed mostly in solutions of structure-disorder cations, such that the water molecules weakly bound around the cations are quasistablized and structured by a magnetic exposure, and the adsorption of the structured ions on the mica surface thickens the adsorption layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetic effect on the adsorption of ions in aqueous solution.
the effects of magnetic exposure on aqueous solutions.
the magnetic effects in aqueous solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic effects on the thickness of the surface layer are due to the magnetic stabilization of water molecules in the vicinity of structure-disordering ions.

the magnetic effects on the adsorption of ions are caused by the magnetic stabilization of the water molecules bound weakly around the structure-disorderings ions, which is the most reasonable interpretation for the present results and the previous ones.
the magnetic effects are not caused by the magnetic field, but rather by the magnetic exposure, which is a magnetic field that has been applied to a solution and then removed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the magnetic exposure can quasistabilize the weakly-bound water molecules around structure-disordering cation and that the magnetic effects on the adsorbed layers are caused by the adsorptive interaction between the structured cations and the surface.
the magnetic exposure in the solutions of Cs+, Rb+ and K+ ions causes the magnetic thickening in the adsorbed layers on mica surface.

we have found a new way of controlling the structure of the aqueous solutions and the adsorbed layers on the solid surfaces, which would have important implications for the understanding of the structure and dynamics of water and for the development of the surface modification technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new technique for the evaluation of the magnetic effects on the thickness of the surface adsorbed layer.
the thickness of the hydrated layer on the mica surface can be increased by magnetic field.
the magnetic exposure thickened the adsorbed ion layer on the surface and this effect was destroyed by the external disturbances, such as stirring and shaking the solution.
